key_insight: A generative image-based model decomposes complex indoor illumination from a single multi-view capture into individual light sources, enabling intuitive per-light editing (on/off, color, intensity) with multi-view harmonization to keep edits consistent and photorealistic.
problem_solved: Removes the need for dense geometry or manual light modeling by enabling interactive, per-light manipulation of indoor scene illumination from a single multi-view capture while preserving multi-view consistency and realism.
method: Generative image-based light decomposition that factorizes scene illumination into constituent light sources across views.
Per-light latent controls to independently edit state (on/off), chromaticity, and intensity for each discovered light.
Multi-view lighting harmonization to enforce consistent appearance across camera views and produce photorealistic recomposed images.
impact: Enables realistic, easy-to-use lighting edits for AR/VR, content creation, relighting datasets, and lighting-aware vision tasks without costly recapture or full scene reconstruction; accelerates workflows for practitioners needing controllable scene illumination.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multi-view capture → light decomposition → per-light controls → recomposed multi-view renderings.
Before/after multi-view panels showing a light toggled off/on and its color/intensity changes across several views.
Per-light overlay (heatmap or icons) on the scene showing discovered light sources and editable parameters.
Small chart or icon set summarizing benefits: consistency, per-light control, single-capture workflow.
paper_title: LuxRemix: Lighting Decomposition and Remixing for Indoor Scenes
paper_authors: Ruofan Liang, Norman Müller, Ethan Weber, Duncan Zauss, Nandita Vijaykumar
